adherence.reason: The story presents a suspicious death, a detective, clues, interrogation, and a culprit-focused reveal, clearly functioning as a mystery.
Elias is the chess club president found dead after the disputed draw, but Mara the detective—not Elias—is the narrative protagonist.
Mara Silvers is explicitly identified as a former Grandmaster who resigned from competitive play years earlier.
The ending explicitly reveals the draw and move sequence as a coded confession prearranged by Elias and his killer.
Nearly all action occurs in the cramped tournament hall, but Mara explicitly steps outside into the night before returning, violating the entirely-within requirement.
The investigation and confrontation unfold continuously during a single rainy evening.
Chess vocabulary and board, piece, move, sacrifice, defense, and endgame metaphors recur throughout the entire story.
The closing scene has Mara replay and recite the final game aloud in order to pressure Julian into confessing.
